v35_scratch unchanged (the shipped FastRiskScore solver) on the fine suite: every numeric column split at its 99 percentiles
g2 + beam children: the 10 best variables by gradient, each at its best threshold (one child per variable) instead of the 10 best columns, which are mostly neighbouring thresholds of one variable
g3 + beam children screened by a 2-D fit (intercept + new point), full refit of the best 2 x beam; one colsum for swap screens; parent design reused in child fits

g2 + one beam child per variable (its best threshold by gradient, picked in numba); children screened by a 2-D fit, full refit of the best 2 x beam; per-variable loops only over rows with a nonzero code
fine_v1 on a chain representation: nested binary columns detected from the data, one ordinal code per chain, all column statistics from per-code histograms (same search)

g2 + one beam child per variable (its best threshold by gradient, picked in numba); children screened by a 2-D fit, full refit of the best 2 x beam; nonzero-code rows only; vectorised column scan, chain codes by binary search on bitsets

g6 with the beam's child screening replaced: every column's gain for every parent is bounded by one Newton step on the new coefficient (gradient and curvature histograms, one pass per level); each parent proposes its 10 best variables at their best column; only the best 2 x beam proposals are fitted
g8 + beam diversity by variable signature: among proposals and among fitted children at most one per multiset of variables (supports that differ only in their thresholds count once)
g12 with the swap screen returning only the picked columns (no dense (columns x values) arrays), and variable signatures built incrementally from the parent's, only for the proposals that are fitted
g13 + ILS starts deduplicated by their score vector (duplicate columns), swap screen by partial selection, move-evaluation buffers sized per variable kind (same search)
g10 with the beam's row weights and Newton gains in numba (x^2 block skipped for binary data), and the ILS swap phase's removal states and second-order screen in numba (same search)
g24 + pair moves at every ILS local optimum: two support points change by one each, evaluated exactly on rows grouped by (x_S, y); accepted moves continue the local search
g19 + chain columns as comparisons, scores in numba, chain codes by a branchless binary search on per-word bits, new beam coefficients warm-started at the Newton step (same search)
g24 + minimum support: every indicator column needs >= sqrt(N) weighted training rows on each side, and two thresholds of one variable in a support must be >= sqrt(N) rows apart (beam and ILS)
h2 with the min-support mask in numba and the ILS value-change candidates picked in one vectorised pass (same search)
h3 with the ILS iteration in numba kernels: value changes + additions, the swap phase (removal states, second-order screen, estimates for all removals) and the exact check (same search)

h4 + pair kicks: after the starts, drop the pair of support columns with the cheapest combined removal and run the ILS again (next pair after a fail, 3 fails); ILS additions screened to 16 columns by a second-order model; beam: sigmoids per row group, Newton tol 1e-4, 15 exact child fits per level; swap phase keeps its removal states

h4 + 2 pair kicks: after the starts, drop the pair of support columns with the cheapest combined removal and rerun the ILS (swap phases only within 0.1% of the best loss; next pair after a fail); ILS additions screened to 16 columns; beam: sigmoids per row group, Newton tol 1e-4, 15 exact child fits per level; swap phase keeps its removal states

h4 + 2 pair kicks (drop the pair of support columns whose joint removal costs least, exactly; rerun the ILS with swap phases only within 0.1% of the best; next pair after a fail) + ILS additions screened to 16 columns; whole ILS run in one numba kernel; beam: sigmoids per row group, Newton tol 1e-4, 15 exact child fits per level

h7 with the beam proposals (per-variable picks, support hashes, signature cut) and the row regrouping of kept children in numba, the kick pair ranking in numba, and the rounding calibrated on distinct score values (same search up to rounding ties)
h8 without the band rule: only the indicator support rule (>= sqrt(N) weighted rows on each side of every indicator); thresholds of one variable may be close
